headline_hook: Anthropic Doubles Claude Usage While Opus 4.6 Goes 1M-Default and Chrome DevTools Gets an AI Brain
preview_topics: Anthropic's capacity surge and Opus 1M upgrade
Chrome DevTools MCP for agent debugging
the jagged frontier of AI-assisted coding quality

pick_of_the_day.thesis: The first rigorous study of AI-assisted code quality in real open-source projects reveals a jagged frontier of its own — speed gains are real but the quality debt compounds silently, and most teams have no instrumentation to catch it until it's already in production.

model_literacy.relevance: Opus 4.6 now defaults to 1M tokens for Claude Code users — but raw context length and how much a model actually utilizes are very different things. Understanding effective context (the portion of the window the model reliably attends to) matters more than the headline number when planning agentic workflows.

items.title: Anthropic Doubles Claude Usage Limits for Off-Peak Hours Through March 27
items.angle: A rare capacity giveaway signals Anthropic has enough GPU headroom to experiment with demand shaping — and wants you building habits during off-hours.
items.key_fact: 2x usage on weekends and outside 5–11am PT weekdays for two weeks

items.title: Opus 4.6 with 1M Context Is Now Default for Claude Code on Paid Plans
items.angle: The opt-in long-context model silently became the default — and the API price didn't budge. Claude Code users just got a massive upgrade with zero friction.
items.key_fact: 1M-context Opus 4.6 default on Max, Team, and Enterprise with no API price increase

items.title: dots.mocr Sets New Open-Source SOTA for Document Parsing
items.angle: An open-source OCR system that nearly matches Gemini 3 Pro on document parsing — finally a viable self-hosted alternative for production pipelines.
items.key_fact: 83.9 on olmOCR Bench, #2 on OCR Arena Elo behind only Gemini 3 Pro

items.title: Anima Trends #1 on HuggingFace with 230K Downloads
items.angle: A new model rockets to the top of HuggingFace trending — community adoption at this pace suggests it's hitting a sweet spot others missed.

items.title: Google Ships Official Chrome DevTools MCP Server for AI Agents
items.angle: The missing bridge between coding agents and front-end debugging just arrived — Google is betting that AI should see what developers see in the browser.
items.key_fact: Official MCP server lets agents inspect, debug, and interact with live Chrome sessions

items.title: Financial Datasets MCP Server Turns Claude into a Live Market Research Assistant
items.angle: Real-time stock data, SEC filings, and earnings via MCP — the kind of vertical data integration that makes agents actually useful beyond code.
items.key_fact: Direct agent access to stock prices, financial statements, and SEC filings

items.title: Apideck CLI Tackles MCP's Context-Window Bloat Problem
items.angle: As MCP tool counts grow, context consumption becomes a real bottleneck — this CLI-first alternative trades protocol elegance for token efficiency.
items.key_fact: Significantly lower token consumption per tool call compared to standard MCP

items.title: Simon Willison Distills How Coding Agents Actually Work Under the Hood
items.angle: The best explainer yet on the mechanics behind coding agents — essential reading before you trust one with your codebase.
items.key_fact: New foundational chapter added to his Agentic Engineering Patterns guide

items.title: Dan Shipper: Coding Agent UIs Need a Main-Chat-Plus-Side-Chats Paradigm
items.angle: Power users are outgrowing single-thread agent UIs — the workflow pattern emerging in practice points to where tools need to go next.
items.key_fact: Main-chat-plus-side-chats is the natural workflow pattern for agent power users

items.title: Skills Files Boost Agent Tool Usage, But Self-Improving Skills Don't Work Yet
items.angle: Manually curated Skills files measurably improve coding agent performance with MCP — but the dream of agents writing their own skills hits a wall.
items.key_fact: Human-curated skills help significantly; auto-generated skills don't improve outcomes

items.title: First Rigorous Study Quantifies the Quality Cost of AI-Assisted Open-Source Code
items.angle: Speed gains are real but quality debt is accumulating silently — the first study with hard numbers on what Cursor-era coding actually produces in the wild.
items.key_fact: Academic study of Cursor AI usage across real open-source projects

items.title: The 'Jagged Frontier' Paper Is Now Peer-Reviewed and Published
items.angle: The study that gave us the vocabulary for AI's uneven capability landscape is now the canonical citation — if you're arguing about AI productivity, this is the paper to reference.
items.key_fact: Now formally peer-reviewed and published after widespread preprint adoption

items.title: HuggingFace Open-Sources WAXAL: Speech Dataset for 19 African Languages
items.angle: A massive gap in low-resource language AI just got a serious dataset — 17 languages for TTS and 19 for ASR, all open-source.
items.key_fact: Covers 19 African languages for ASR and 17 for TTS

items.title: Stop Sloppypasta: The Grassroots Revolt Against AI Content Slop Gains Steam
items.angle: The backlash against undifferentiated AI-generated content is organizing — a signal that the market is about to start pricing quality differentiation.
items.key_fact: Campaign gaining significant traction on Hacker News

items.title: Why Most AI CLI Tools Are a Security Nightmare for API Keys
items.angle: The industry automated the coding workflow without fixing secrets management — and everyone running coding agents should care.
items.key_fact: Fundamental security hygiene gaps in how AI CLI tools handle API keys

items.title: Bindu Reddy: GPT-6 Will Be Trained by GPT-5.4, Compressing the Cycle 10x
items.angle: A concrete timeline claim for recursive self-improvement in model training — speculative but worth tracking as the meta-learning loop tightens.
items.key_fact: Claims 10x compression of the training cycle via recursive AI-assisted training

items.title: Tsinghua Open-Sources OpenMAIC: A Multi-Agent Interactive Classroom Framework
items.angle: A concrete multi-agent architecture for education you can actually fork and build on — not a paper, a working framework.
items.key_fact: Open-source multi-agent classroom system from Tsinghua University
